comments.text:
I am insurance agent. 
Counter point mentioned karne he muje regarding this video.
1) kya India me log personal finance ko leke knowledge rakhte he?

2) kya sabko sare financial instruments pata he?

3) MF and stock ki volatility se sab comfortable he?

4) I agree Liquidity is big concern in insurance policy but logo me  jis instrument me liquidity he log us instrument ko bech k apani temporary requirements to Puri kar lete he. But compound effect ka magic miss kar dete in long term. 
Insurance me mostly koi surrender nhi karta policy ( company aur agent unko manane ka try karte he long term k liye invested rehene k liye)

5)Mostly 8%-9% ka return to mil hi jata he client ko par product me jisme unka capital guaranteed hota he. 8% - 9% is good return jinhe market se dar lagata he.

6)Agent ko 15-30% commission milta he ispe bura man ne ki kya baat he? Agar me jada commission kamane k liye logo k piche pad rha hu. Aur aise logo se investment kara raha hu jo jindagi me kabhi investment karne wale nhi the. 

For eg. aaj hi maine ek policy bechi he jisme husband is not serious about investment aur wife ko apne bachchi k padhai aur shadi k liye paise jama karne he. 1 month se piche padhke Maine unka investment kara diya. It's win win situation for both muje commission ne motivate rakha itne lambe samay tak unse follow up lene me. Aur bachche k naam pe kuch investment to ho gayi.

7) Ulip wohi customer kharid ta he jise market ka knowledge hota he. Market ki volatility se comfortable hota he. 
Agar koi customer long term k liye ulip aur mf same amount dalta he aur same portfolio choose karta he .
E.g nifty 50 portfolio choose karta he. 
Charges k vajese ulip 1-2% hi sirf Kam return dega. Mostly customer term insurance prefer nhi karte he itna awareness nhi he logo me.
So in that case agar shuruvaati dino me hi customer ko kuch ho jata he to mf sirf invested money hi dega par ulip insurance cover bhi dega.
Isliye log 1-2% kam return hone k bavjud mf se jada ulip ko pasand karte he.

8) jaise ki apne thumbnail me likha ulip me paise dalne k badli paisa jala do. 
Ek kaam karte he aap 1 lack jala do aur me 1 lac ulip me dalta hu. Dekhte he kiska return achcha aayega.

Me agree karta hu insurance aur investment alag alag hona chahiye. But on ground aap logo ko educate karne jaoge koi samajta nhi he.
Insurance agents ne bada role play kiya he logo ko unke personal finance k bareme sochne.

For those who are revising it in 2026, please find below a Master Prompt with the insights as discussed in above video. Throw it to any AI along with the policy doc/web link of the plan to make it crystal clear what the Plan is effectively Offering. The prompt being named "Sanchay Minus Audit" being dedicated to @LLA Mandeep Bhai!


____________________________
The Master Analysis Prompt
____________________________
Role: You are a Senior Financial Forensic Auditor and Master Investment Analyst. Your goal is to perform a "Sanchay-Minus" audit on a new financial product to determine if it is a wealth-creator or a wealth-destroyer
.
Instructions: Analyze the provided financial plan across the following six dimensions, drawing on the logic of Internal Rate of Return (IRR), opportunity cost, and insurance sufficiency as defined by expert financial critiques.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Phase 1: The "Cold Coffee" Anatomy (Product Type)
Identify the Hybrid: Does this plan combine Life Insurance and Investment?
.
Naming Convention Check: Does the plan use "power words" like Guaranteed, Double Income, Cash Back, or Assured Wealth to mask its underlying structure?
.
Commission Incentive: Based on the plan type (e.g., Endowment), estimate the likelihood of high agent commissions (approx. 25%) being the primary driver for its sale
.
Phase 2: The Insurance Sufficiency Test ("The Ehsaan Check")
Sum Assured Ratio: Calculate the ratio of the Annual Premium to the Sum Assured. If the cover is only ~10x the annual premium, categorize it as "Insignificant/Ehsaan"
.
The 10x Income Rule: Compare the life cover offered to the user's annual income. If it is less than 10x (ideally 25x), flag it as a failure for family security
.
Premium Comparison: Compare the premium of this plan to a standard Term Insurance plan for the same cover. If the cost is 5x-10x higher, mark it as "Grossly Overpriced"
.
Phase 3: The IRR Forensic (The Truth of "Double Income")
Cash Flow Mapping: Map all outflows (premiums as negative values) and all inflows (payouts, bonuses, maturity as positive values)
.
Calculate the IRR: Use an Internal Rate of Return calculation. If the result is between 4% and 6%, explain how it fails to beat inflation and is "an investment joke"
.
The Bonus Trap: Identify any "declared bonuses." Check if these bonuses are liquid or locked until maturity without earning additional interest. If locked, calculate the inflation-adjusted "real value" of that future bonus
.
Phase 4: The Tax & Inflation Mirage
Tax Benefit Evaluation: Analyze the "Tax-Free" claim. If the IRR is below inflation, explain why tax-free status is irrelevant (since no real profit is being made)
.
Indexation Comparison: Compare the plan's returns against debt instruments that offer indexation benefits
.
Phase 5: The "Golden Handcuffs" (Liquidity & Surrender)
Surrender Value Analysis: Calculate the loss if the user exits the plan after 3, 5, or 10 years. If the loss exceeds 50% of the principal, label it a "Wealth Destruction Trap"
.
Opportunity Cost: Compare the maturity corpus of this plan against a 10%–12% SIP in a diversified Mutual Fund over the same period. Quantify the "Lost Crores" due to time-value-of-money
.
Phase 6: Final Decision & Ranking
Rank the plan on the "LLA Shoddy Scale":
Level 1: Pure Term/Pure Investment (Recommended)
Level 2: Sub-optimal Hybrid (High costs, but some utility)
Level 3: The Sanchay Minus Category (6% IRR, poor cover)
Level 4: The Wealth Destroyer (Heavy surrender penalties, bonuses losing to inflation, <5% IRR)
Final Verdict: Provide a "Yes/No" recommendation based on whether the plan prioritizes the company's greed over the customer's financial independence
.

comments.text:
Hello Boss
You are not showing the perfect analysis 
If I had to be in your place I would calculate IRR in a different manner as you are not calculating IRR a correctly 
If you are getting 12 lakh cover in Max product then you have to deduct the cost of a term policy for 12 lakhs for the age for that category. So IRR a will jump to 6.5% at least
The FD will give 8% then the post tax return will be 5.4% which is 1% less. Talk about guarantee then you should understand that in 2001 LIC had launched an annuity plan with 12% interest Jeevan Dhara. Do you know that even today people are still getting 12%. But you were not born that time and you don’t remember it. We should have a 30% component in guaranteed money back which may be golden opportunity if interest rates  drop. Your father did not need a policy which is clear but people will think insurance is not required 
Term plan lapses if the premium is not paid after 15 days. You don’t know about claim concession where in LIC policies death claim is settled even if premium is not paid for 6 months in 4th and 5th year, for 12 months in the 6th to half term of the policy and for 18 months if premium is not paid. Death claim is settled by deducting the outstanding premium. This benefit is not available in term policy. So reality is buy 30% in endowment guaranteed plan and the rest in MF and term policy for 10 to 15 years

comments.text:
Hi Dileep - Pls don't confuse investment with Insurance. 

Immediately cancel these nonsensical schemes. The agents will try their best to prevent you from cancelling as they receive life long commissions by selling these kind of schemes.  There is a 30 days cooling period of cancellation so make use of this time and put your money in the right place.  Remember, the only people getting rich in these kind of schemes are the banks, insurance companies and their agents.

 I would recommend you do the following:
1. Park 6 months of monthly expenses as emergency money in a easily breakable FD. Preferably in your wife's account so that there is no tendency to spend this corpus 🙂
2. Take a pure term insurance for yourself and your spouse if she is also working. Preferably 10-15 times your annual income.
3. Take up a pure health insurance scheme at the earliest, preferably a family floater scheme. The earlier you take up one, lesser will be the premium. Again don't mix this with investment. 
4. Once the first three points are taken care of, then invest in those asset classes that you understand.
5. Lastly you would need to continuously learn and upgrade your financial skills to avoid being hoodwinked and duped by these banks and their agents.
Good Luck!

comments.text: Why does noone show how Insurance Agents themselves  do an ``Application Filling Up fraud''. In India KYC is required for takin health Insurance. An executive of Insurance company fills up ur forms. Very cunningly he deliberately projects you as healthy, concealing your pre existing diseases. Beacuse the Sales Firms are front for actual Insurance companies . The Insurance companies give these `Agents ' upto 75% of first premium and then 20-33 % on each subsequent premium. So the aent , knowing that you have some disease and the Insurance Company is going to reject your form, shows you as FIT . You are insured. Problem comes after 3-5-7 years when you claim as for some operation etc. The claim is rejected on the ground that you lied to insurance company about your pre-existing illness. And you are blamed . Courts dont listen because you have signed the form and if they listen , it will be 25 years later when you are dead 2 times over. So please read and fill up the form in your own hand absolutely disclosing every illness. MUST DISCLOSE YOUR SMOKING AND DRINKING TOO OTHERWISE YOUR CLAIM WILL BE REJECTED.

Aree Bhai ek baat bata, jab 6-6.5% ka Guaranteed return mill raha hai for over such a long period toh then how is it not better than as an alternate to Secured Bonds like government bond.

You're saying you get indexation benefit on capital gains on bonds okay, but you will get capital gains on bonds only if the interest rates fall in the future. 

Now if you sell your secure bonds in the future when the interest rates have fallen, the money which you will get as part of your secure portfolio, now if you reinvest that money in secure bonds, you'll get a lower return because interest rates have fallen.

Now if the interest rates rises in the future the value of your bond will fall then you would not sell your asset anyway.

and most likely you'll hold the bond till maturity and in that case, considering a government bond, you will get around 7.5% coupon which after a 30% tax slab comes to around 5.25% which is lower than 6% ot 6.5% of tax-free return.

 Also, let's say you have to invest  10 lakh Rupees in your safe part of the portfolio, with 1 lakh each year
What is the Guarantee that each year at the time of your investment the G-Sec rates would be around 7.5%, it may rise or fall but it is the risk that you're taking.

It is easy for "financial influencers" to show only one side of the coin. Would love to discuss with you on this further if you're willing to

comments.text:
Here is my 2 cents:

While I completely agree with msg in te video. I want to explain why I have taken a similar plan. And would I like to know what is your take on it.

So there are people who only believe in doing FDs rest everything is evil and greedy for them.  Though my father always diversifies his investments (stock market, mutual funds, endowment plans etc) he maintains that one should atleast have 10-15 lakhs in FD.

So till last year I had 2 lakhs in FD and was going to create more FD, but my banker gave a suggestion and I am listing it out below in short:
1. FD return in around 4.5 to 5
2. If you are planning to not touch this savings for next 10 years.
3. Than instead of doing FD you can go for such plans where nothing additional you will get in terms of returns but you will get a life cover.

I got here point, I am planning to create 10Lakhs FD in next few years and if returns are same (in FD it may get Below 4% like in US where it is practically 0 now)  I get additional life cover.

Yes it's expensive and name of this plans are misleading but it's a good alternative if you are planning  to go for FD.

Also since you get payouts every year, you might not be tempted to use all the Money at once (this continuous stream of money every year would ensure I pay for my child's education from it.)

It will be wise choice if you know the pros and cons of the plan and your risk appetite and it's management strategy

comments.text:
Bro, seems like you need to learn more about financial markets. This plan is sold less as an insurance policy but more as an investment policy. In insurance, company uses the whole pool of money to pay the death benefit but here the company has to return the money with interest every month. In order to do it, they invest in fixed income securities like bonds. When these bonds are matured, the amount is paid to the investor as annuity. 
How will the company pay a huge death benefit when the money is already invested to generate annuity every year. 
The other thing is, we all know that fixed income products are hardly generating any returns these days, be it FDs or debt or liquid mutual funds. So from where will the company provide 7-8% returns. 
And if you are such an expert financial advisor you must know that  every financial plan is designed for a specific need. Here the need is regular income. So if the client is getting 6% guaranteed returns, which is still better than FDs, so what's wrong in it? As far as lock in period is concerned, investor is well aware about it before he takes the plan. 
If the company applies your logic, there is a high chance that the company will default at some point of time. And all the investor's money will be lost.

comments.text:
I am insurance agent. 
Counter point mentioned karne he muje regarding this video.
1) kya India me log personal finance ko leke knowledge rakhte he?

2) kya sabko sare financial instruments pata he?

3) MF and stock ki volatility se sab comfortable he?

4) I agree Liquidity is big concern in insurance policy but logo me  jis instrument me liquidity he log us instrument ko bech k apani temporary requirements to Puri kar lete he. But compound effect ka magic miss kar dete in long term. 
Insurance me mostly koi surrender nhi karta policy ( company aur agent unko manane ka try karte he long term k liye invested rehene k liye)

5)Mostly 8%-9% ka return to mil hi jata he client ko par product me jisme unka capital guaranteed hota he. 8% - 9% is good return jinhe market se dar lagata he.

6)Agent ko 15-30% commission milta he ispe bura man ne ki kya baat he? Agar me jada commission kamane k liye logo k piche pad rha hu. Aur aise logo se investment kara raha hu jo jindagi me kabhi investment karne wale nhi the. 

For eg. aaj hi maine ek policy bechi he jisme husband is not serious about investment aur wife ko apne bachchi k padhai aur shadi k liye paise jama karne he. 1 month se piche padhke Maine unka investment kara diya. It's win win situation for both muje commission ne motivate rakha itne lambe samay tak unse follow up lene me. Aur bachche k naam pe kuch investment to ho gayi.

7) Ulip wohi customer kharid ta he jise market ka knowledge hota he. Market ki volatility se comfortable hota he. 
Agar koi customer long term k liye ulip aur mf same amount dalta he aur same portfolio choose karta he .
E.g nifty 50 portfolio choose karta he. 
Charges k vajese ulip 1-2% hi sirf Kam return dega. Mostly customer term insurance prefer nhi karte he itna awareness nhi he logo me.
So in that case agar shuruvaati dino me hi customer ko kuch ho jata he to mf sirf invested money hi dega par ulip insurance cover bhi dega.
Isliye log 1-2% kam return hone k bavjud mf se jada ulip ko pasand karte he.

8) jaise ki apne thumbnail me likha ulip me paise dalne k badli paisa jala do. 
Ek kaam karte he aap 1 lack jala do aur me 1 lac ulip me dalta hu. Dekhte he kiska return achcha aayega.

Me agree karta hu insurance aur investment alag alag hona chahiye. But on ground aap logo ko educate karne jaoge koi samajta nhi he.
Insurance agents ne bada role play kiya he logo ko unke personal finance k bareme sochne.

It's win win situation for both muje commission ne motivate rakha itne lambe samay tak unse follow up lene me. Aur bachche k naam pe kuch investment to ho gayi.

7) Ulip wohi customer kharid ta he jise market ka knowledge hota he. Market ki volatility se comfortable hota he. 
Agar koi customer long term k liye ulip aur mf same amount dalta he aur same portfolio choose karta he .
E.g nifty 50 portfolio choose karta he. 
Charges k vajese ulip 1-2% hi sirf Kam return dega. Mostly customer term insurance prefer nhi karte he itna awareness nhi he logo me.
So in that case agar shuruvaati dino me hi customer ko kuch ho jata he to mf sirf invested money hi dega par ulip insurance cover bhi dega.
Isliye log 1-2% kam return hone k bavjud mf se jada ulip ko pasand karte he.

8) jaise ki apne thumbnail me likha ulip me paise dalne k badli paisa jala do. 
Ek kaam karte he aap 1 lack jala do aur me 1 lac ulip me dalta hu. Dekhte he kiska return achcha aayega.

Me agree karta hu insurance aur investment alag alag hona chahiye. But on ground aap logo ko educate karne jaoge koi samajta nhi he.
Insurance agents ne bada role play kiya he logo ko unke personal finance k bareme sochne.

comments.text:
Life Insurance major objective is to cover Risk of life i.e Risk related to death... But Mutual Fund or other investments option are variable and also subject to market risk which doesn't come with life risk coverage. 

So life insurance is only for the purpose of covering your life not to earn return from it. If we are getting less return from any life insurance policy along with life coverage risk then whats wrong with it ?

If a person died before maturity of the policy then his family can get sum assured but is this possible in mutual fund or other investments in case of death ?

Hence Life Insurance policy major objective not to earn return but to cover our risk. So every person should have Life Insurance coverage irrespective of what interest they are going to earn from it.

comments.text:
This is a great video but you didn't consider one thing, the insurance associated with the premium. To calculate the returns based on the sum insured and the amount you get is not that straight forward. There are two scenarios first if the person dies before maturity, and the other where the person lives till the maturity of the plan. Here the calculation is based on just the assumption that the person is alive till maturity if you add the other part in the equation it will give you the actual returns for the plan which will be considerably more.
If you look at the returns or the insurance amount in isolation they are bad, but if you look at it together they are really not that bad for someone having a very low risk appetite.
I am not adding the calculation because it requires to take into account life expectancy at different age and can be confusing, but if someone is interested I can add it.

Hello sir, happy to see you typing , that you are doing CA . I also hope your father has good health.
I must say that your father has made very nice decision, i want you to ask your father that at the time of policy login what was his sole aim behind opening this policy.
I am pretty sure that he was very concerned about your FUTURE with or without his presence.
Also ask him that ,agent talked about term insurance or not..
Endowment policy returns are not comparable to any non guaranteed investment products, Endowment plans ment to be your future provisions.
I am very surprised to see that your father has taken very small amount of insurance as well as your education provision. And his planning is not sufficient. 
But still its not a bad one.something is better than nothing. 
I'm very sure that you also don't want to take any risk in your child's education planning by mob mentality. It certain event and should be planned by guaranteed results.

There is difference between return on investment and return of investment. 
MF AND STOCKS ARE NOT EVEN GIVING INVESTED AMOUNT BACK.
yes there are possibilities of good returns but in endowment plan there is  Guaranteed returns on investment. 

I also congratulate you that your father is survived in this world to make you comment like this.
Imagine , god forbid if your father faced any unwanted events what would be your situation , ask this to your respected mother too. That how would she raise you alone without your father. Will you be able to do CA  now if that whould have happened.??

We cant feel Breadwinner's absence until it is real.

Also ask your insurance advisor to do your financial planning once i am sure that he will not let your expectations down.
Majorly why they give small amount of insurance is that they are not listened properly. 

I am sure you will understand the importance of life insurance in your life. 
We should have term insurance first 25 times of annual income ,also endowment policy for the certain future events we can not take risks in.
I.e. education provision and retirement provision.
Thirdly make emergency fund.
After that if any investment you want to do you can invest in MF and EQUITY.
IT comes at last.
Not first otherwise your financial pyramid will fall down.

I am sorry if i hurt you in any way.but this was important to say.

Also dont trust this type of Youtubers they are promoting wrong things for their own income.

comments.text:
@dhavalvaghela8263  I understand what you're trying to convey!

I was just making a point that there's a lot of other good investment plans with better returns compared to this.

You were right when you said my father wanted secure investment without any risk and guaranteed returns but I was saying that this plan gives 3-4% annual return which doesn't even best the inflation, and majority of benefits are being enjoyed by the agents and company itself.

Being from finance background I have invested money with huge returns on equity and mfs, because I had a good knowledge about it, but a common man doesn't know a lot about money market so they prefer these preplanned investment schemes!

I'm not saying my father had committed a mistake by investing in endowment policy, at that time it might have been best decision.
But in the current situation, these policies are worthless, everyone goes for term plan or any other schemes.

I respect your feelings, but I'm not fully wrong,  you can easily calculate the returns you'll get from these policies and compare it with any index funds, even after being risky, index funds will always beat the returns of endowment!


Regards.

These agents will say maturity amount or bonus is not taxable as per 10(10D), but according to 10(10D) section c, if the premium paid in any financial year is more than 10% of sum assured then maturity or bonus is taxable, that means the amount 20 lac or something you get at the end you have to show as income from other sources in your Income-tax return and pay 30% tax on that. Invest in stocks instead and even after capital gains, of more than 1 lac it is just 10% tax.

comments.text:
This video looks interesting in the beginning. But if you deep dive it tries to show life insurance companies in poor light ,especially all the endoment or money back plans. Nothing short of sensationalism. Negativity sells. Sells fast, so this video looks interesting to those who dont like insurance company,plans and  agents. But pity its not a fact.
Insurance companies are regulated by IRDA and how is it possible to get a shock.
Endowment plans do give returns with protection. In India, people view insurance as expenses, not an essential one. InsuranCe penetration in India is very very minimal. Vast majority of population dont have insurance. Some people are still relyctant to take term plan as they see no benefit on survival at the end of policy term. So ensowment plans which gives money back.
And surely this is not investment.
At the same time this video presenter feels that only term plans are worth taking. But if one term plans are offerred by insurance companies, NO INSURANCE COMPANY will survive in long term which will lead to death of industry.Insurance works on pooling of risks concept. So to cover one term plan ,how many members are required to contribute ?
And this author bats for mutual funda SIP and stocks which are risky and people some times may end up losing whole capital. So this is ok, but not insurance plans which guarantee returns although ROI / IRR is less..
And author speaks only from urban educated financial literates point of view. How many in our family will understand SIP DEBT MARKET AND MFs?
Insurance endowment plans are one of the class of assets for an investor but not ONly class of asset.

1. Guaranteed plans are not Insurance plans. The insurance part is there to make it tax free as per current tax rules. 
2. Yes the surrender value is poor if one wants to pre-terminate the policy. Hence invest if you know u can continue. 
3. Also you are comparing this policy with mutual fund which is wrong. The right comparison of this Guaranteed plan is Fixed deposits. The IRR will be comparable to FDs (FDs offer shorter duration but income is taxable). Also for a person who wants some portion of investment in guaranteed (as diversification) will find this useful especially if he falls in highest tax bracket, which will take the IRR to approx 8.5% for such plans. Which is good given the current interest rate enviroment.

I am insurance agent. 
Counter point mentioned karne he muje regarding this video.
1) kya India me log personal finance ko leke knowledge rakhte he?

2) kya sabko sare financial instruments pata he?

3) MF and stock ki volatility se sab comfortable he?

4) I agree Liquidity is big concern in insurance policy but logo me  jis instrument me liquidity he log us instrument ko bech k apani temporary requirements to Puri kar lete he. But compound effect ka magic miss kar dete in long term. 
Insurance me mostly koi surrender nhi karta policy ( company aur agent unko manane ka try karte he long term k liye invested rehene k liye)

5)Mostly 8%-9% ka return to mil hi jata he client ko par product me jisme unka capital guaranteed hota he. 8% - 9% is good return jinhe market se dar lagata he.

6)Agent ko 15-30% commission milta he ispe bura man ne ki kya baat he? Agar me jada commission kamane k liye logo k piche pad rha hu. Aur aise logo se investment kara raha hu jo jindagi me kabhi investment karne wale nhi the. 

For eg. aaj hi maine ek policy bechi he jisme husband is not serious about investment aur wife ko apne bachchi k padhai aur shadi k liye paise jama karne he. 1 month se piche padhke Maine unka investment kara diya. It's win win situation for both muje commission ne motivate rakha itne lambe samay tak unse follow up lene me. Aur bachche k naam pe kuch investment to ho gayi.

7) Ulip wohi customer kharid ta he jise market ka knowledge hota he. Market ki volatility se comfortable hota he. 
Agar koi customer long term k liye ulip aur mf same amount dalta he aur same portfolio choose karta he .
E.g nifty 50 portfolio choose karta he. 
Charges k vajese ulip 1-2% hi sirf Kam return dega. Mostly customer term insurance prefer nhi karte he itna awareness nhi he logo me.
So in that case agar shuruvaati dino me hi customer ko kuch ho jata he to mf sirf invested money hi dega par ulip insurance cover bhi dega.
Isliye log 1-2% kam return hone k bavjud mf se jada ulip ko pasand karte he.

8) jaise ki apne thumbnail me likha ulip me paise dalne k badli paisa jala do. 
Ek kaam karte he aap 1 lack jala do aur me 1 lac ulip me dalta hu. Dekhte he kiska return achcha aayega.

Me agree karta hu insurance aur investment alag alag hona chahiye. But on ground aap logo ko educate karne jaoge koi samajta nhi he.
Insurance agents ne bada role play kiya he logo ko unke personal finance k bareme sochne.

comments.text:
It is not getting compounded. That's what i said in my last video- CAGR.
The NAV of 100 might very well become 50 after a few years, and that is a risk one must take while investing in MF. 

However, historic data and a lot of facts suggest that if you hold the investment for long term, 10, 15, 20 years, the NAV will almost always get increased by a significant amount, generating a CAGR of at least 12% (maybe more but we always like to assume the reasonable). 
Though it won't compound, it would still look like a compounded investment @12%, is what i mean.


Conclusion: The longer you hold, the lower your risk gets

ELSS are not bad, if you compare a good ELSS (say Mirae tax saver) with any good performing large cap fund, you'll find a lot of stocks common in them. 

I think you can consider ELSS for discipline as well returns.

About PPF, it may generate low returns but those returns are tax free. However, If your EPF is already covering 1.5 lakh, then it's pointless to invest in PPF in your own name. But if you invest PPF in your spouse's name, or kid's name, then it makes sense. 

Other options for lock in investments could be bonds, watch my bonds where i explained them in detail.

comments.text: What people don't understand is that an average 6% tax-free return is very good. It seems low in today's term but over 30 years it's actually great. Think about it. In the next 30 years, markets will develop, interest rates will go down, returns from stock markets will also normalize to lower levels, and of course, as an economy develops, inflation goes down as well. So don't just argue straightaway saying that 6% is very low. Look at the long time horizon for which they are giving you such return, and all other factors. By the way, even I have term insurance and I will never go for endowment, but still, new-age products like Sanchay Plus are competitive enough.

There are two ways.. You can go about it.. 
1. Surrender and accept what they are paying you back as surrender value..  This is the most preferred one solution.. 

2. Ask them to convert it into paid up policy.. So whatever you have paid so far.. It will have proportionately benefits.. 
You will not need to pay any premium anymore. 
The small insurance cover will remain as long as policy is active. 
And very small amount of maturity you will get at the time of maturity.. 
This way you can avoid loss on premiums paid.. But remember in the long run n as per inflation it won't be a good idea..

comments.text:
Market Linked Plans doesn't provide Insurance. Do you get ₹. 5 Lakhs , if you shell out just ₹. 50000 on SIP , and you die immediately thereafter ....?? In fact the money you spend will be doomed. There is a difference between Insurance Plans and Investment Plans. Both are necessary for a Person, to be financially prudent. The Rate of FD's are dipping. An FD which used to earn 12-13% earlier has dipped to around 5-6% now. And there too , in case of an eventuality , only upto  ₹. 1  Lakh is insured. In future, it's going to be reduced further to 2-3%. Moreover one has to renew it after every 5 Years. In Insurance Plans, you lock the premium at the present Rates for upto 50 years  or till death...!! 
I am not accusing you, despite being a Financial Advisor for many years now, you haven't surrendered the Policy of your father. You are telling that , you are going to close it ...why ?? 
Coming to Shares .... The Markets have ups and downs...!! You have heard people commiting Suicides , after investing in Shares, BUT NOT AFTER INVESTING IN INSURANCE COMPANIES ...I think. 
You are right , Share Markets offer 12 - 13 % returns , but without the Insurance factor which I pointed out earlier. Some Shares drain off all the money invested too ....!! Moreover there is a Tax on the Returns too , both in FD and Shares ....!!!! If you deduct all these factors , what would be the effective IRR of FD / Shares ....?? 
Ihave commented as a layman. Pl. correct me , if I am wrong.

comments.text: Even I thought about it for a while, if term insurance is remarkably affordable then why aren’t people buying it (just 1k INR a month for ~1Cr coverage). Especially, basic businessman who can easily afford to pay premium for a 5/10Cr insurance coverage. So this is what I believe goes in their mind, a basic business man’s business allows him to make huge profit once in a while, so instead of improving his lifestyle, he prefers buying land in the outskirts (stable % ROI) of their city for each of his family member one at a time (whenever he makes huge profits) & leave it as a long term investment. Eventually, all his dependents are technically property owners at some point of time, which also means they are financially stable, therefore term insurance(health insurance is an exception) no more fall in their priority as they already have land for financial security & stability. Moreover, lack of knowledge regarding term insurance and not enough faith in the company to return the sum assured could be a potential drawback.

comments.text: Agree sir. Term plan has max benifit but if we survive for 30-35 years which we have 80% chance of doing then what? aajkal youtube par wealth increase karne ka ek golden rule har youtuber bta raha hai ki Mutual Fund me investment karo aur 1 crore ka term insurance le lo aur ho gayi aapki wealth planning.
Ab term insurance ko ek example se samajhte hai:
Example:
Suppose 1 Crore ke term plan ke liye premium hua 25,000 yearly. ek company 1 year me 10,000 logo ko term plan sell karti hai to uske pas total premium aaya = 25,000 x 10,000 = 25 crore. Inme se agar maan le ki 0.5% logo ki death ho jaati hai to 10,000 x 0.5% = 50. 50 logo ki death hoti hai to company ko claim liability amount hua 50 x 1 Crore = 50 Crore. Aur company ke pas fund aaya tha 25 Crore. to ab ye baaki ka 25 Crore company kaha se degi?

Fir company apna brahmastra use karti hai "force majeure" clause. jisme baaki bache hue logo ki family lapete me aati hai aur fir wo lagate hai court ke chakkar. toh bhai saab jara iss reality ke baare me apne bataya hi nahi.

Ab raha mutual. fund Frenklin Mutual fund ne apne 6 debt scheme covid-19 ke time par kyu band karne pade. kitne logo ko nuksaan hua mutual fund me. logo ko 10-12% ke return ka lalach diya jaata hai fir overall return 6-7% hi reh jaata hai or kayi baar to itna bhi nahi milta. mutual fund ki reality aap log intni imaandaari se nahi batayenge jitni imaandaari se aapne endowment plan ke baare me bataya. 

agar koi life insurance plan leta hai aur unfortunately  uski death sirf ek premium dene ke baad hoti hai to uski family ko 50-60 lac ka amount diya jaata hai jiska premium 50-60k hota hai aur aise hundreds of cases hote hai jisse bohot si family ko support milta hai. iss situation me kon si FD plan ya kon sa mutual fund hai jo aise support karega? term insurance ki reality maine upar btat hi di hai.

ab aate hai apke logic par ki agent ko endowment plan bechne par commission milta hai to bhai saab apke logic ke hisaab se to apko kisi bhi actor ki movie nahi dekhni chahiye kyoki wo apke paise se hi crorepati bnaa hai. apko ambaani adaani ke koi bhi product ya service use nahi karni chahiye aap d2h ya internet recharge karte ho lekin apko ads dikhaye jaate hai aur paisa aap de rahe ho. apke paiso se hi bohot se log crorepati ban gaye hai. hai koi logic isme?...yes insuranace agent ko commission milta hai isliye wo ye kaam karta hai verna wo ye kaam kyo karega? ye kya logic hua ki endowment plan me insurance agent ko mota commission jaata hai? apne ye to bata diya ki 25% tak jata hai lekin apne ye nahi bataya ki ye sirf ek baar jaata hai uske baad 5 % jaata hai. aap ke biscuit ka packet lete hai to usme bhi ke bohot bada profit margin hota hai lekin aap waha question hai karenge kyoki apko waha logic nazar aata hai lekin insurance agent ko milne wale commission me apko koi logic nazar nahi aata.

I agree that don't put all eggs in one basket. mutual fund bhi sahi hai, share market bhi sahi hai FD plan bhi sahi hai aur endowment plan bhi sahi hai. sabka alag alag purpose hota hai. apke hisaab se chalte to LIC of India aaj hoti hi nahi jo govt ko itna bada support karti hai. aur bohot se public sector yaha tak ki apke share market me ek bohot bada hissa LIC of India ka hai or ye sab isliye hai ki log saalo se endowment plan lete aaye hai. apke hisaab se jitne bhi logo ne endowment plan liya hai wo sab bewkoof hai aur LIC of India itni badi organization isi bewkoofi ki wajah se bahi hai.

jitni aapki income hai usse 100 times jyada income karne wale logo ne bhi LIC ke plans me paisa lagaya hai aur laga bhi rahe hai to wo bewkoof hai. aap itne samajhdaar hai to iske hisaab se to apko ab tak Rakesh jhunjhjhun wala ke barabar hona chahiye tha. aap to expert hai investment ke isiliye aap youtube par itna gyaan baat rahe hai wo bhi one sided hokar.

bohot se logo ne apne endowment plans ko band karke mutual funds me paisa lagaya or apna paisa duba bhi baithe ye bhi reality hai.

And yes I am an insurance agent. apne sirf one sided hokar ye video banaya isliye mujhe itna lamba post likhna padha taaki logo ko dono sides pata chale. Logo ko 1% ka huge profit wala mutual fund to nazar aate hai lekin usme 99% chupa hua risk nazar nahi aata.

comments.author: @ClasherJay

comments.text:
Here's my final response point by point:

1. just because there is a product that offers you insurance + investment doesn't mean you can expect the same thing from other products like Mutual fund. why should a mutual fund give you a life insurance just, tell me why? 

2. some of the mutual fund 2 of a life insurance along with the login of escape but I personally don't like that option. I would rather go for a mutual fund that I am confident with, for the sole purpose of making my money grow and building wealth for future. 

3. there are very good Mutual Funds are available in the market that can give you even more than 10% returns but I was being conservative. it's only a matter of financial literacy and awareness. and for people who don't have this I recommended paying a professional and getting a financial plan made. Dude, even if you invest in index funds you will easily get 10% and even more. 


4. Only elss Mutual Funds have a lock in of 3 years and also with a good purpose. You get the advantage of section 80c of the income tax act. Even then 3 years is a very short duration. 

5. I have told this in multiple videos that Mutual Funds do have a charge it's called expense ratio and if you buy a direct mutual fund instead of a regular one you will reduce this charge by a huge margin and end up saving more money or should I say making more money. Index funds (passively managed, minimum risk) have an expense ratio as low as 0.1%. 

6. another charge is called exit load which only apply is if you withdraw your money within one or two years of investment. I absolutely have zero problems with discharge because it goes away from 2nd or 3rd year in most mutual funds. besides if you can't even keep your money for one or two years then maybe you are not made for investing. 

7. You have let your expectations rise unnecessarily.  insurance companies offer you a product which is a combo of insurance + investment and you just by it thinking that it is giving you double benefit but in reality you are not realising that you are also paying extra amount for that extra benefit and your actual investment is pretty less. 

this has made you to demand a free of cost Life Insurance with Mutual Funds which is unrealistic. You want a life insurance go by a life insurance and if you want investment, go invest separately. 

8. What about the risks? you asked: the more you educate yourself the less risk you will have to take and higher the chances of you building a great wealth. if you research for even one hour, I guarantee you will end up finding Mutual Funds with minimum risks. One I have already told you about. 

9. Finally, I find it very stupid to choose a life insurance company for purpose of investing. 

I just find it sad to write the same things over and over again for people like you who don't even have the patience to understand full video especially when it's not an entertainment video but actually is a very important video that affects your financial discipline and future. If you don't help yourself, nobody will.

like I said, I don't want anyone to blindly trust me please feel free to research on your own and verify the facts that I have mentioned in this video and in this comment

comments.text:
Let me share something i shared last year on another youtube forum.
I thought of carrying out an independent analysis of the HDFC sanchay policy benefits. The policy brochure provides an illustration that coincided with a query in that youtube forum a year ago.

Here is the query,
“Madam, I got a sample illustration from Hdfc life Sanchay plus.. Plan option: long term income 1 lakh invested for 10 years.. From 12 th year to 35 th year we get 1 lakh/ yr. On 36 yr you get back 1000000 which you invested earlier + 100000 of that year.. Total benefit. 3500000”


So, we have got,
Premium per year = 1,00,000; Sum Assured = 12,50,000; Nos. of years payment term = 10; Age at start of policy = 30 years (assumed);


First phase – Investment through advance premiums for 10 years
As per HDFC website, mortality charge for pure insurance is based on age and sum assured at risk. So, for a 30 year old, insurance charge can be 1.0555*1250000/1000=1,320. Note that this amount keeps decreasing as the premiums keep increasing.
Considering HDFC life’s service charges + agents commission, we can assume a total expense of 5000 per year. So, net amount actually invested = 1,00,000-5,000=95,000.


A very important note is that I will be using 6.5% rate of interest/return for my calculations. Generally, endowment insurance plans give returns in this range.


I used this website for compound interest calculation https://financialmentor.com/calculator/compound-interest-calculator


Using 95000 as advance 1st payment and subsequent 9 payments, we have,
Total investment = 9,50,000; Compounded annual rate of interest = 6.5%; Hence, Total value at start of 10th year = 9,50,000+3,38,007=12,88,007/-


Second phase – Rest phase upto start of 12th year
I used this website for lumpsum compounding 
https://www.motilaloswalmf.com/tools/compounding-magic-lumpsum
The above lumpsum amount 12,88,007 will continue to accrue interest. Compounded annual rate of interest = 6.5%; Final lumpsum value of investment at start of 12th year = 14,60,880/-


Third Phase – Disbursement of benefits since start of 12th year to 36th year
This is a simple example of deferred annuity plan. Here, the lumpsum amount accumulated above will be disbursement as annuity for the next 25 years.
I used this website for annuity calculation https://www.annuitycalc.org/
Principal amount at start of 12th year = 14,60,880/-
Annual compounded rate of interest / growth rate = 6.5%;
Annuity amount = 1,00,000/-; Number of years to receive annuity = 25 years;
And you wont believe, lumpsum amount available at the end = 10,66,862/-


That sums up the whole analysis. As you can see, the results are similar to the benefits of HDFC Jeevan Nischay plus. You can check the calculations through the websites and let me know if I have made any error. Now, you can see that under all the big announcements of getting lakhs of rupees for 25 years, its simple calculation and the rate of return is a mere 6.5%. 


Lets take another scenario, where we separate insurance and investment (which is logical). The total available amount is same as before at 1,00,000/- annually.
First, buy term insurance of 1,00,00,000/- (1 crore) for annual premium of approx. 10,000/- (check with website).
I will invest remaining amount as SIP of Rs. 7500 for 10 years in ELSS mutual funds. 
Total investment = 9,00,000; Rate of return = 12% (conservative)
Amount at start of 11th year = 17,42,543; Amount at start of 12th year = 19,51,648;
Systematic Withdrawal payment term = 25 years
Rate of interest of annuity = 8% (Considering SWP in the same ELSS)
Annuity starting from the 12th year = 1,70,000/- annually
Net annuity (After paying term insurance premium+LTCG) = (1,70,000-100000)*0.9+1,00,000-10,000 = 1,53,000/-
Lumpsum amount available at end = (13,39,460-1,00,000)*0.9+1,00,000=12,15,514/-


The second scenario also provides all the 3 benefits – insurance, investment & taxation. 
Lets compare the two,
Benefits    HDFC Jeevan Sanchay +  Term insurance+ELSS
Sum assured   12,50,000 (12.5 lakhs)  100,00,000 (1 crore)
Net investment   9,50,000                           9,00,000
Actual insurance premium 5000*10=50,000          10,000*36=3,60,000 (over 36 years)
Net Annuity           1,00,000 per year                 1,53,000 per year
End lumpsum amount  10,00,000/-                  12,15,514/-

People must be financially aware before investing their hard earned money in fancy brochures and sales pitches regarding lifesaving policies and tax benefits. Insist that your advisor or agent gives a detailed calculation. If the agents are financially literate, they will provide you with the justification; else, they will tuck their tales and run away. After all, it is our money.
Good luck to all. Happy investing and saving.

Amazing Video Bro 👍 PLEASE READ THIS. Took me sometime and efforts to write this.

I have a something to say here. We get 5 - 6% of Interest which you somehow suggested to be bad and compared with FD instantly. 

# Now pls tell me what is max IRR you would get in FD, max 5.6 or let's say 6% right ? 

# As we all now FD is Taxable so if you deduct the tax your IRR on FD is ever lesser than these plans 

# Having flexibility to redeem the investment is not always good according to me, we all know to achieve something in life one must be dedicated and deciplined; and having such flexibility can trigger you to redeem the investment. For eg: Majority of people redeem their Mutual Fund investments in first 2 years which they finalized after a lot research and know would give them at least 10% of IRR if they hold for longer duration but do they hold ? We all know the answer.
But when you know your investment is locked and can't be redeemed, you might face temporary difficulty in life but then your end goal won't be defeated. People usually make provision for temporary difficulties bcz they know there's no other option so they have to but due to this flexibility they won't make extra effort to make other provisions hence end up redeeming this. We all know this.

# Since FD doesn't provide life cover even for a rupee and offer same IRR, isn't it better to go for one of these plans ? They provide some life cover, even if it is 2 lacs but that's free no. You aren't paying anything extra and getting the same IRR as FD.

# Bro inflation would be there in FD as well no ? So with same IRR in both plans, how come FD returns are better and how would be beat to inflation?

# Add on point on inflation: Bro when we will be paying our contribution in next 10-15 years, our own investment will also be having the inflation effect no ? It's not that you receive 20lacs as maturity that its value would be 15lacs then, bro it's with our investment also no. When you'll pay 1lac of contribution over 10-15 years, the value of your 1lac will also be lesser no in practical terms like 95k for first then 90k for second and so on, bcz inflation is anyways increasing. Plus why do we forget that our incomes would increase over time. 

# Bonus: The bonus you mentioned is entirely wrong bro, pls recheck. It is much higher than you advised, actually it's double the amount you invested. Eg: you invest 10 lacs and get bonus of 11lacs

# Calculator: Bro you did not adjusted the amount here with inflation whereas you have been giving example of decreased money value due to inflation repeatedly

# Also when you earn 10lacs extra, you pay 3lacs as tax only bro. Your IRR goes lesser in that case. And you would 10lacs only IF mutual funds returns are 10% everyyear which is not guaranteed bro we all know this. Plus there are many more factors with mutual funds, one is people keeps on checking the growth regularly and that brings a lot of tension at times. Taking tension for 10 years might cause a big health issue, you never know. I know you might not find this a logical reasoning but this is what happens in society bro, it's 100% practical.

comments.text:
Insurance is purely for security purposes, It should never be considered as an investment option. It is the buying behaviour of customers because of which such products are developed by companies, they always expect something in return, that's the reason term plans are not so popular. But even if the customer is getting just 1rs extra, it gives a feeling to them that they are earning profit, thus they are happy to make that purchase. 
While purchasing a life insurance policy, always think what happens if you die, never think what happens if you survive, if you're thinking on that line you will be making a wrong buying decision. 
There are 2 kinds of risks which life insurance  covers. 
1. The Risk of Dying Early 
2. The Risk of Living too long

These basic needs can be covered with Term plans, Annuities and Pension plans. 

Every thing this guy spoke is on point.
I am an Insurance Student myself, can't agree more.
